# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventy-six  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper and former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P20](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0020), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Uncle Jim  <sub>[v4 c9 P19](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0019)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim was a tall, stooped, and ungainly old man, yet suggestive of great strength. He had a clean-shaven, deeply lined bronzed face, a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders, and deep-set blue eyes. Though considered plain and homely, his countenance was beautified by his inner spirit.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015)_

## Personality

Captain Jim was a high-souled, simple-minded, and exceptionally gentle man who possessed a chronic habit of enjoying life and remaining cheerful. He was uncommonly deferential and chivalrous toward women, refusing to allow a bad word against any woman to be said in his presence. Possessing the natural talent of a born storyteller, he delighted in recounting his many seafaring adventures and discussing deep philosophical questions. He was also extraordinarily kind and generous, even starving himself to feed a passing stray dog.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P13](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0013), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P23](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0023), [v4 c6 P25](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0025), [v4 c9 P49](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0049), [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059), [v4 c14 P3](../source/v04-c14.md#nw-v04-c14-p0003), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)_

## History

Captain Jim was a lifelong sea captain who spent decades travelling the world and experiencing countless adventures, including shipwrecks, mutonies, and pirate attacks. Over fifty years ago, he lost his beloved Margaret when she drifted out to sea and perished in a storm. He eventually retired from the sea to become the lighthouse keeper at Four Winds Point. When Anne and Gilbert Blythe moved into the old house of dreams, Captain Jim welcomed them warmly and quickly became a cherished friend and regular visitor. He introduced Owen Ford, the grandson of his old friend John Selwyn, to his cherished handwritten journal, the "life-book." Together, Owen and Captain Jim collaborated to write a novel based on Captain Jim's life and his romance with Margaret. Shortly after receiving the very first printed copy of his published book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P0](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0000), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c9 P30](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0030), [v4 c17 P21](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0021), [v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016), [v4 c24 P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030), [v4 c25 P3](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0003), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v4 c39 P25](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0025), [v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Sailed all his life until five years prior to meeting the Blythes  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- Lost his true love, Margaret, at sea over fifty years ago  <sub>[v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016)</sub>
- Rescued his cat, the First Mate, from a tree nine years prior  <sub>[v4 c9 P42](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0042)</sub>
- Was a lifelong friend of John Selwyn, the old schoolmaster of Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c7 P2](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0002), [v4 c25 P7](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0007)</sub>
